name: history and corpus
reason: The corpus is the repo's biggest asset and it is used as a list rather than as evidence. Advisory identifiers, severity scores and exploited-in-the-wild status are named. Nothing measures silent patches, incomplete fixes, link rot or how much of the record nobody has read, which are the questions that decide whether a completeness claim means anything.

L16-009.note: Membership in the exploited in the wild list is a binary oracle, which is the factor stated as a check.

L16-001.note: One identifier source is named. Overlap and coverage across databases is not measured.

L16-006.note: The weakness taxonomy is the artefact a label reliability study would use.

L16-007.note: The scoring system is the artefact a bias study would use.

L16-008.note: Exploit prediction is the closest thing to availability timing and it is a score, not a measurement.

L16-039.note: Reading the shipped code is how a patch diff would be interpreted. No entry does diff analysis.

L16-041.note: A technique taxonomy gives a denominator. It is not the deduplicated count.

L16-056.note: A test item traceable to a real finding, or marked as written from theory.

L16-061.note: Each source's licence recorded against how it will be used is the copyright constraint.
